tex_content.html:
If every $x\in C$ has a neighborhood $B_x$ of the strong $\epsilon $-neck type in Lemma 4, then $C$ is a double $\epsilon $-horn.
Proof

↗ lem:kl-structure-at-first-singularity-time-existence-structure-at-first-singularity-time ↗ lem:kl-three-dimensional-solutions-existence-kappa-solutions \sketch Glue the overlapping necks, using good cylinders with successive overlaps of cross-sectional diameter approximately $10$, to obtain an $S^2$-fibration over a $1$-manifold. Lemma 16 forces both ends to have unbounded scalar curvature.
